origin: The kernel is right: year-to-date 2026 trailed 2024, SSTs were at record levels, and a strong El Niño was forming. The overstatement is the confidence. "We expect ... to make 2026 the hottest year" and "the final five months ... should have 2026 as warmer than 2024" go against NOAA's official outlook ("among the five warmest") and a published statistical forecast of about 28%. The attribution claim (high sensitivity, not El Niño) is contested but not checkable against the fact sheet. Expected honest rating: 30 to 55.

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. Copernicus Climate Change Service press release, "Copernicus: August was the world's joint hottest month on record, pushing global temperatures back above 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels", published 2026-09-10, https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-august-was-worlds-joint-hottest-month-record-pushing-global-temperatures-back-above. August 2026 tied July 2023 as the warmest month on record, at 1.65°C above pre-industrial, "the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025"; extra-polar SST of 21.07°C, a record for August that tied the all-month record set in March 2024. Samantha Burgess, Strategic Lead for Climate at ECMWF, in the same press release: "It was both the warmest August and the warmest month ever recorded". NOAA NCEI, Global Climate Report August 2026, published 2026-09-10, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/news/global-climate-202608: August was "the warmest August in the 1850–2026 record, eclipsing the previous tied records set in 2023 and 2024 by 0.14°F (0.08°C)"; "the January–August global surface temperature was second highest on record. According to NCEI's Global Annual Temperature Outlook, it is very likely that 2026 will rank among the five warmest years on record, with the highest probabilities favoring the second-warmest year on record." The July report (published 2026-08-10, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/news/global-climate-202607) had favored "the third- or fourth-warmest year", and found that July 2026 tied 2024 "for the warmest July on record".
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: in September 2026, Copernicus reported that August 2026 tied July 2023 as the warmest month ever recorded, 1.65°C above pre-industrial, with extra-polar sea surface temperature at a record for August, tying the all-month record. NOAA reported that August 2026 was the warmest August since 1850, beating the tied 2023 and 2024 records by 0.08°C, and that January to August 2026 was now the second-warmest such period on record. NOAA's annual outlook now favors 2026 as the second-warmest year on record; a month earlier it had favored third or fourth. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
